title: List multiples of a number and find common multiples

lesson.title: Multiples and Common Multiples

steps.say: You already know your four times table, so you already know multiples — a multiple is just an answer in that times table. Today we learn how to list them and then spot the numbers that show up in two lists at once.

Imagine hot chocolate at the winter market costs four dollars a cup. One cup is four dollars, two cups is eight, three cups is twelve. Keep going and you get the multiples of four. On a hundred chart, just start at four and hop four squares each time.

visual.caption: Multiples of 4: start at 4, hop 4 each time

steps.say: Now a bag of mini donuts costs six dollars. One bag is six, two bags is twelve, three bags is eighteen. So on the chart we start at six and hop six squares each time to list the multiples of six.

visual.caption: Multiples of 6: start at 6, hop 6 each time

steps.say: Here is the fun part. Look at both lists and find the numbers that appear in both. Twelve is in both, twenty four is in both, and thirty six is in both. Those are called common multiples — amounts you could spend exactly on hot chocolate or exactly on mini donuts.

Careful with one mix up. Some kids say twelve is a factor of six. That is backwards. Factors are the small numbers that fit inside six, like one, two, three and six. Multiples of six are the big ones that six climbs up to, like six, twelve, eighteen and twenty four. Factors stay small, multiples grow.

visual.caption: Multiples of 6 climb UP the chart — factors stay small

steps.say: So to find common multiples, list the multiples of each number, then circle the ones that show up in both lists.

lesson.answer: Multiples are the answers in a times table — the numbers that appear in both lists are the common multiples.

practice.question: Picture a hundred chart in your head, or draw the numbers one to thirty on paper. First circle every multiple of five up to thirty, then circle every multiple of three up to thirty. Which numbers get circled twice?
practice.answer: Multiples of five: five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty five, thirty. Multiples of three: three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen, eighteen, twenty one, twenty four, twenty seven, thirty. The numbers circled twice are 15 and 30 — the common multiples.
